Lucy Letby - Cross-examination Day 8: Babies M & N
CONTENTS
MS LUCY LETBY (continued)
Cross-examination by MR JOHNSON (continued)
Wednesday, 7 June 2023
(In the presence of the jury)
MS LUCY LETBY (continued)
Cross-examination by MR JOHNSON (continued)
Mr Johnson.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: On Monday, before the midday adjournment, we dealt with pretty much the whole of three cases: [Baby K], [Baby F] and [Baby L]. Is there anything that you said about any of those three children that you, on reflection, wish to amend?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And so far as the wider case is concerned, in other words questions that I have been asking you since we started this exercise, is there anything that you wish to amend?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you give that some thought at the end of each day, that issue?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So you -- it's not a criticism at all, but you reflect on the evidence you have given?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: As much as I can remember, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes, and you think about whether or not there's something that you have said that, with hindsight, you might either wish to change or re-emphasise or add to or take away from?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. And each time I have asked you that question, you have confirmed that, in effect, there is nothing you wish to change?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Thank you. Now, if we can move on to the case relating to [Baby M], please, who is named in count 16 on the indictment. I'd like to start, as I have done from time to time, with your defence statement. All right? The jury now have a typed copy of the statement.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The part I'd like to ask you about starts at paragraph 137, which in the jury's copy is page 17.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I've dealt with parts of this already because, as we see from the document, this section of it concerns both brothers, [Baby L] and [Baby M]. All right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So on Monday we dealt with the parts that refer simply to [Baby L] --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- and we will turn now to [Baby M].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: At paragraph 137 you say that after the twins were born on 8 April, they were put into nursery 1, that you and Amy Davies took them there, and you looked after them on their first day, you had looked after [Baby L] and Amy looked after [Baby M].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And I asked you some questions about that on Monday so far as [Baby L] was concerned.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: At 138 you say:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "[Baby M] was not put in a proper space. He was slotted into a space by a wall with a portable Masimo monitor. He was fitted in this way because nursery 1 was full."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You say.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You then move on to say that:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "We put a crash call out. [Nurse B] came and tried to turn the incubator around to get [Baby M] on to a proper monitor."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Sorry, where are we now?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: 146, I beg your pardon. We've moved on. 139 to 145 relate to [Baby L]. My mistake.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You just check for yourself that I've not missed anything out between 139 and 146.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: (Pause)
It just refers to -- about [Baby M], about the Neopuff on the wall at 144 and 143.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right, okay. You're quite right. 143:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "[Baby M] collapsed as Mary and I were making up fluids for [Baby L]. His alarm went off so we went over to him and he was apnoeic. When I look back, I'm not sure if he wasn't breathing or whether he'd had a desaturation."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Then you say:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I used the Neopuff that was on the wall, but because of how [Baby M] had been fitted into the nursery it wouldn't reach the cot and the mask pulled off. Someone brought me a new Neopuff mask."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "We asked Belinda Simcock and Ashleigh Hudson to do the bag for [Baby L] while we dealt with [Baby M]."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So the bag in that context of course is the more concentrated dextrose that Mary Griffith had started to put together?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And then:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "We put a crash call out [this is the bit where I had jumped to]. [Nurse B] came and tried to turn the incubator round to get
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: [Baby M] on to a proper monitor. Dr Jayaram then came in and probably other doctors. Eventually, we moved [Baby M] to the intensive care side of the nursery because we needed a ventilator."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You then say at 147:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I didn't notice any change in skin colour in [Baby M], although I have not dealt with many sick Asian babies, so I may not have been accustomed to the changes in skin colour. However, no one mentioned any changes in skin colour at the time."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You then say at 148 you took care of [Baby M] once he came off the ventilator:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "He'd been given medication prior to his collapse. I can't recall if it was me or Mary Griffith who did this."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And you then turn back in the document to [Baby L] at 150 and 151.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Then 152:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Sometimes when we do a resuscitation we write notes on whatever is available. This would sometimes be a paper towel. That is happened [it maybe should read 'that is what happened'] with [Baby M]. I wrote notes on the paper towel which then remained in my pocket and ended up at home with me."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I just want to understand what you're saying.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I have asked you some questions about this and I will return to it, but I just want to understand what it is you're actually saying in the document there.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Are you saying in the document that once you had written notes on the paper towel it went into your pocket and that is where it remained until it got home?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm saying that I wrote notes on the paper towel, yes, and at the end of the day it came home with me in my pocket.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And where had it been in between?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Well, it would have been used during the shift to write up notes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: All right. We'll come back to that.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "A number of my diary entries were written retrospectively, for example 'Twins resus'. Matters like this were written after I'd been removed from the unit. I was documenting matters that I believed might be significant. LD stands for long day."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And that's how you deal with the case of [Baby M] in this document.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Was there anything that was particularly memorable about [Baby M] so far as you were concerned?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The delivery of the twins stood out in my mind because that was the first delivery I'd been to where I was the allocated nurse for a baby by myself, so yes, as a pair of twins, yes, they stood out in my mind, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I want to see whether you agree with a number of propositions. All right? First, that [Baby M] was born in good condition?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That within a few hours his observations were being taken every 2 hours and he was breathing for himself in air?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, if that's -- I obviously can't see the chart now, but yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Okay. Well, if you want to look at the chart, please don't let me rush you beyond it if you want to. They're all behind divider 16 in that bundle that you have in front of you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm doing my best to reflect accurately the evidence that's been given, but it may be that I from time to time I can make a mistake. So if you want to check anything, you say so. All right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: But do you agree with those propositions?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Could you repeat the last one?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes: obs every 2 hours, breathing for himself in air; that's within a few hours of his birth.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: He was not an intensive care baby, was he?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Um, no, I don't believe he was at this time, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: No. Is it your case that the staffing levels generally caused or contributed to [Baby M]'s collapse?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't know what caused [Baby M]'s collapse, but the unit was very stretched that day with staffing, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes, but you will understand, I'm sure, that it has been suggested on your behalf from time to time, and you gave evidence in answer to questions from your own counsel from time to time, that may have been taken as suggesting that there is a connection between staffing levels and collapses. All right? And I hope you understand that what I'm trying to do is to look at each case individually and see whether in fact there is a connection on your evidence.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So putting to one side for a second the fact that you have told us that you don't know what the cause of [Baby M]'s collapse was, are you suggesting that there is a positive association between staffing levels and his collapse?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think that's a potential, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, a potential -- what is the potential connection?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Because I don't know exactly what happened to [Baby M], but I know we were very stretched that day in providing all of the needs on the babies on that unit to make sure that they were all cared for. It was very stretched for every child --
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: But are you --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: -- and [Baby M] wasn't in a correct space either.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Are you pointing to a positive event which, had staffing levels been different, would have been dealt with differently?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Potentially, yes, if [Baby M] had been in a proper space and we hadn't been as stretched with staff, maybe things would have been acted on quicker, I don't know.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What difference would the space have made?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: He wasn't on a correct monitor. He wasn't -- he was just in a corner space, which isn't ideal. We don't usually have babies in that space.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, we'll come to the population distribution in a moment. But you are postulating the possibility, are you, that had he been on a Philips monitor there may have been an earlier alarm than in fact there was?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Potentially, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. That doesn't have anything to do with staffing levels, though, does it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That's to do with the monitor.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So at the risk of repeating myself, just going back to the staffing levels, what are you suggesting is the connection?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Again, I don't know what happened to [Baby M], but as nursing and medical staff we were very stretched that day. Um... Sorry, can you -- what was I saying, sorry?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I'm looking to giving you an opportunity, really, of telling the jury what you are suggesting is the connection between staffing levels and [Baby M]'s collapse.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: As I say, I don't know what happened to [Baby M], but the unit was very busy that day, staffing wasn't at a great level, the doctors were very busy, as were the nurses.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Potentially, babies on the unit at that time didn't have such close monitoring as maybe they would have done if there'd been more staff or less babies.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Are you suggesting that anybody's mistake contributed in any way to [Baby M]'s collapse?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't know what caused [Baby M]'s collapse.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So is the answer no?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Are you suggesting that medical or nursing competence made a contribution?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Again, that's hard to answer when I don't know exactly what happened to [Baby M]. I know he had had a few issues earlier on in the day. Maybe that could have been dealt with differently, I don't know.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. Well, when we get to them, if you are suggesting that things should have been dealt with differently, will you say so, please --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- and tell us what the difference could or should have been; yes? Thank you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Now, I'm sure you will remember that Dr Jayaram told us of discolouration that he saw on [Baby M] at the time of his collapse.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I want to put to you his description and ask whether you disagree with what he says; okay?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What he said was this, it was on 22 February if anybody wants to check:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Because [Baby M] was darker skinned, it was more obvious. He was generally pale, which one would expect in a cardiorespiratory arrest. There were patches of very bright pink or certainly more obviously pink because it was on a darkerskinned background on his torso that flitted around. These sort of pink blotches for want of a description, better -- patches. It would appear and disappear and then other ones would appear and disappear. I noticed them on his abdomen because that's the most obvious bit of his body that you could see because the rest of his body had people covering his chest, doing CPR. I noted them sort of when I got there during the start of the resuscitation. I can't comment on how long they continued to be there. Once circulation was restored and his heart rate came above 100, they vanished."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And he said he'd never seen that type of a discolouration before [Baby A]. Okay?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you agree with his description?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I did not see anything like that, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Did the lighting in nursery 1 make it difficult to see?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Because you've told us, haven't you, that the lighting in nursery 1 is bright?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: This was a daytime collapse.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And so the lighting would have been on full, wouldn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Um, it wouldn't have been on full, no, because no nursery light is on full unless you're actually doing a procedure. But yes, it would have had a fair level of lighting, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is resuscitation a procedure?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, the lights would have been turned up then, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Sorry, I thought you meant during the day.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I'm talking about when Dr Jayaram speaks of having seen what I've just recounted to you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember what you said to the police about the lighting in this particular case?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that it was poor where -- the space that [Baby M] was.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Mm. If we just go to your interview, it's in bundle 2 of the interviews and it's the [Initials of Baby M] section, which is about halfway through. [Initials of Baby M] for [Baby M]. Go to page 4, please, [Initials of Baby M] 4. It's the first of the [Baby M] interviews. Do you have an independent memory of saying this or have you been reading your interviews to see what you said before I ask you questions about it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I have a direct memory of that event and needing to move [Baby M] into a different space.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right at the bottom of page [Initials of Baby M] 4, you're asked a question:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Question: Do you know why he was desaturated?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Answer: No.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Question: So when you attended to him there was nothing obvious that had caused this desaturation?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Answer: Not that I remembered, no. And then that officer says — a different officer says:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Any more questions?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And you give a reply, don't you? Would you just read your reply, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I do remember that his colour was a little bit harder to assess with him being an Asian baby and also he was in a corner space where there's poorer lighting."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So were you suggesting to the police in this interview that the poor quality of the lighting during the daytime in nursery 1 may have been a reason why you didn't see a change in colouration?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. So at the time that [Baby M] collapsed, the nursery was not in full brightness, so when I went over to [Baby M] he was in a darker corner of the nursery.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: But a much lighter corner than nursery 2?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You know what I'm going to say, don't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. What am I going to say?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That I was able to see [Baby I].
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes, in the dark.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. Well, not in complete darkness, but...
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So this time, you're saying that although a nursery was in daytime with the lighting on, the lighting wasn't good enough for you to have been able to see a change in colour?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, it was harder for me to assess because I was not used to caring for Asian babies, so the colour change, if any, was
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: very difficult for me to see. I did not notice any colour change.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I want to turn to the population layout, please, at tile 83, Mr Murphy. We can put the interviews away now, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Here we can see that there were four children in nursery 1.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: How many spaces are there in nursery 1?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Four.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Why was it necessary to put [Baby M] in a corner space if there are four spaces and four children?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The procedure is because we are an emergency unit, there always has to be one incubator free --
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I see.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: -- because obviously we don't know what might come through from delivery ward. So there is always a space set up that's available for any admissions.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Okay. So is this a situation where, as you have told us, because [Baby M] was not an intensive care baby, he didn't actually need to be in nursery 1 at all?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, there was just no room on the outside nurseries, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes, we can see the layout there, can't we?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We see that you were responsible for GT and TSB?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And that your friend Mary Griffith was responsible for [Babies L & M]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: As you have told us, four children in nursery 2, three of whom being looked after by Ashleigh Hudson, one by [Nurse B].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: [Nurse B] had a second child in nursery 4, who was in there with three others, being looked after by Angela McShane, and then Belinda Williamson had the three children in nursery 3.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Was the capacity at the time 16?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So making the allowance for the emergency provision of a single ITU space, you were running, in effect, at capacity?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember describing Mary as quite a junior member of staff, Mary Griffith?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: How many years' experience did Mary have?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't answer that, but Mary only did band 5 roles intermittently. She was predominantly a nursery nurse on the unit and would sometimes go up to a band 5 on days when we were short-staffed, so she wasn't predominantly a band 5 at all times.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Moving on to tile 88, please, do you remember Dr Ukoh saw [Baby M] at 10.25 on the ward round?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Did you have anything to do with [Baby M] at this stage?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I couldn't answer that, I don't know.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: All right. Let's look at what you were doing at the beginning of the shift, if we can. Keeping that on the screen, but if you just put away those interviews, please --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's not the interviews.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That's not the interviews? What's that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's the second jury bundle.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: It's the first one actually, but do you want to just put that one away as well. If we could get out the black neonatal review, please, so it's the second neonatal review
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: bundle, and turn to the [Surname of Babies L & M] section of that. It's the third document in there.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: On the front of it, it says:
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Events 17 and 18: [Baby L] and [Baby M]."
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Do you have that?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: On the second page you have the layout we've just seen on the screen.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And then on the third page, we have what in effect is a summary of other activity with other children going on at about this time.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If we go to page 4 to deal with the time at which Dr Ukoh was looking at [Baby M], the notes of which we have on the screen, we see blue typescript showing what you were up to at about this stage.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Just turn back a page to page 3, please, which is the first page of the table in effect. We see you doing observations for GT, don't we, at 8.30?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Some medications at 9.05 to 9.11 --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- between lines 29 and 32?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Also checking some medications for AW who was in nursery 2, being looked after by Ashleigh Hudson?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Then going to page 4, lines 44, 49, 58 and 66, are you doing observations, feeding and making a note relating to the child TSB?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Who was one of your two children in nursery 1?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: The child GT was, if this document is correct, which we believe it to be, very low maintenance; would you agree?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Let's look at how GT was occupying your time then. At line 22, so back to page 3, do we see you feeding GT --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- at 9 am? That's the first thing you did on the shift that's been recorded by you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.

blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Answer: I don't remember."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Then over the page, just at the bottom of that page:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Question: Just in your experience, Lucy, the fresh blood, what can cause that?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Answer: Is this when he was first born?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Question: No, this is on the 15th.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Answer: So any sort of trauma to the airway."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is what you said. Is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "He's having some sort of an abdominal issue, an abdominal bleed, something like that. If the tube's been -- the NG tube's been inserted forcefully, it can cause a bit of trauma going down."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is that true?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Which part? Well, yes, it's all true, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is it true that the NG tube can cause bleeding in the throat or the mouth?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, a small amount, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember it being suggested to Dr Evans on your behalf that that was a ridiculous suggestion, that the NG tube —
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: For a very large amount of blood, yes. Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember the expert evidence of Elizabeth Morgan, the expert nurse, which was agreed?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Not in the entirety, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That any unusual occurrence should have been escalated verbally to the medical staff, particularly where it was relevant to a particular issue to which the blood was relevant. So a haemophiliac child bleeding.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You didn't escalate it, did you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I cannot say that I didn't escalate it verbally.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You were telling your friend [Dr A] about it, though, weren't you? Do you remember?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, I remember at some point [Dr A] asked me how he was.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Let's just look at tile 199, please, which is a Facebook message you sent him at 11.29. Read that out, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's your message.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Small amounts of blood from mouth and 1ml from NG. Looks like pulmonary bleed on X-ray. Given factor VIII. Wait and see. Apnoeas have improved and gases good. Colour and perfusion still not great. If deteriorates, will try to intubate."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: As a matter of fact, the X-ray had been at 09.08, which is well before your record of the blood, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The 10 o'clock, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. If we go back to tile 176, please. This is the reason for the -- this is an X-ray taken at 09.08, reported on by Dr Wright, the radiologist:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Presumed haemophilia A. Profound desaturation and blood at oropharynx on intubation [query] pulmonary haemorrhage."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That was the reason for the X-ray; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So that was [Dr A]'s reason for commissioning the Xray?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: But Dr Wright's report says the appearance is more in keeping with infection than with pulmonary haemorrhage.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. This information comes some time after the X-ray, though, it's not available at that time.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So I'm suggesting to you that you were creating the impression with your colleagues that [Baby N] had a problem which, if it existed at all, was being caused by you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No. Can you rephrase that, please?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. I'm suggesting two things. Either there wasn't a problem at all and you were making it up, as evidenced by the fact you didn't report it through the normal chain of command, or, if there was a problem, you were causing it.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I disagree with both.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember [Baby N]'s parents arriving?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Not in clarity, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, you referred to it in a text message you sent to your friend [Nurse E].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Tile 232. Sorry, that's her question to you, actually, 232. 13.51, please:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Baby G's parents been in?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Asks your friend.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And your response comes 3 minutes later at 13.54, tile 235, please. So [Nurse E], had she gone off from the night shift?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So she would have gone, what, some time after 8 o'clock and probably before 9 o'clock; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So [Father of Baby N]'s statement is correct that they came into the NNU as a result of a phone call?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, they did attend, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember him saying in his statement that -sorry, [Father of Baby N]. Do you remember him saying in his statement that they went to get something to eat?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember what he said happened when they went to get something to eat?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That there was a deterioration with [Baby N].
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: [Baby N] collapsed again.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: To be fair to you, he puts the time of that in the statement as earlier than the time of the collapse; okay?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: But he says such was the dramatic and extreme nature of the collapse that they were offered a priest; do you remember that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And therefore that has to be, doesn't it, the collapse at 14.50?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, if that's the time of the collapse, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, let's look at tile 244, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Your note?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "Desaturation to 44. Heart rate below 100 at 90. Fresh blood..."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So more fresh blood?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "... noted from mouth and 3ml aspirated from NG tube."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So the source, on the face of it, not the stomach -not the lungs, I should say, because the NG tube is in the stomach.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What had you done to [Baby N] to make him bleed?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I hadn't done anything to him.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: This is very similar to what happened to [Baby E], isn't it? Do you agree?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Um, [Baby E] had significantly more blood, but yes, he did have fresh blood, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember telling Dr Mayberry about this?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: It's tile 245 in his note if we look at that, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: If we scroll down, please, Mr Murphy, it's the entry made at -and up a bit, sorry.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think that's Dr Saladi.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That's Saladi, yes. Let's find Dr Mayberry. There he is at the bottom, Mr Murphy was right. This is written in retrospect of course:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Crash bleeped to NNU due to sudden desaturation following 3ml aspirate of blood from NG."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So we're talking about the same event, aren't we?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "1 attempt at intubation by myself. Cords seen but obstructed by swelling in airway."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember what he said about that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I remember him saying it was unusual, he'd not seen anything like that before.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Exactly:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Unlike anything I had encountered previously."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You had shoved some foreign object down [Baby N]'s throat, hadn't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Absolutely not, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That's why he was bleeding.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: [Dr D] saw swelling in the throat.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Dr Brearey saw blood in the throat about this time.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Right? Do you remember?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Um, yes, if that's what he said, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And it's all your work, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, it's not at all.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember some assistance having to be called from Alder Hey?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And you were agitated by that, weren't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, I'd never known anything like that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Mm.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It was -- yeah.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Did you think eyes from outside might work out what you'd been up to?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No. There was nothing to do. I wanted them to come and help [Baby N] because at that point nobody on our unit could do that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember saying to [Dr D], "Who are these people"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "Who are these people?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, I did. I had no idea who these people were. The nursery was full of people and I didn't know who they were. I'd never experienced staff coming from another department or another hospital before.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So that's your reason, is it? You didn't know who they were?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I didn't know who they were, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You didn't know where they'd come from?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I knew where they'd come from, I didn't know who they were or who was doing what. I have never known staff come from different hospitals or different departments.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: It was a completely new experience.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember the evidence from the doctors that as [Baby N] collapsed the final time, they were all away from him?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: As in every doctor?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. Dr Potter and Dr Lakin were in a different room, preparing Dr Potter's equipment, I think, and Dr Gibbs said they were in effect in a huddle, discussing what they were going to do.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And that was the point at which [Baby N] collapsed again, wasn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And you took advantage of, as we have seen in many other cases, them being distracted to try to kill him?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Because kill him -- you did try, didn't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.

blocks.speaker: JOHNSON
